subject: Vocabulary
topic: One Word Substitution II — Single Word for a Phrase (W11 B2)

questions.stem: A person who is unable to pay his debts
questions.explanation: B is correct. INSOLVENT = a person who cannot pay their debts; legally or financially bankrupt. Specific to inability to pay debts (legal/financial context). Trap: Destitute = extremely poor (no money at all, not necessarily debt-related); Pauper = a very poor person, historically one dependent on public charity; Mendicant = a beggar (solicits alms).

questions.stem: A place where bees are kept
questions.explanation: B is correct. APIARY = a place where bees (and their hives) are kept. Root: Latin 'apis' = bee. Trap: Aviary = a large cage or enclosure for birds (root: Latin 'avis' = bird); Aviculture = the practice of keeping and breeding birds; Kennel = a shelter for dogs.

questions.stem: The practice of having more than one husband at the same time
questions.explanation: B is correct. POLYANDRY = a form of marriage where a woman has more than one husband simultaneously. Root: Greek 'poly' (many) + 'andros' (man). Trap: Polygamy = general term for multiple spouses (either direction); Polygyny = a man having multiple wives (Greek 'gyne' = woman); Bigamy = illegally being married to two people simultaneously (not specific to direction).

questions.stem: A doctor who specialises in treating diseases of the skin
questions.explanation: C is correct. DERMATOLOGIST = a specialist doctor who treats diseases and conditions of the skin. Root: Greek 'derma' = skin + 'logos' = study. Trap: Neurologist = treats nervous system diseases (Greek 'neuron' = nerve); Cardiologist = treats heart diseases (Greek 'kardia' = heart); Ophthalmologist = treats eye diseases (Greek 'ophthalmos' = eye).

questions.stem: A speech made without prior preparation
questions.explanation: B is correct. EXTEMPORE = a speech or performance done without preparation or rehearsal; impromptu. Root: Latin 'ex tempore' = out of (the) time (= on the spot). Trap: Soliloquy = an act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone (or as if alone, in a play); Eulogy = a speech praising a deceased person; Monologue = a long speech by one person (can be prepared or scripted).

questions.stem: A person who walks in sleep
questions.explanation: B is correct. SOMNAMBULIST = a person who walks around while asleep; a sleepwalker. Root: Latin 'somnus' (sleep) + 'ambulare' (to walk). Trap: Insomniac = a person who cannot sleep (root 'in-' = not + 'somnus' = sleep); Somniloquist = a person who talks in their sleep ('loqui' = to speak) — this is a very close trap; Narcissist = a person excessively self-admiring.

D is correct. DEMOCRACY = a system of government where power rests with the people (directly or through elected representatives). Root: Greek 'demos' (people) + 'kratia' (rule). Trap: Theocracy = government by religious authority ('theos' = god); Aristocracy = government by a privileged upper class ('aristos' = best); Plutocracy = government by the wealthy ('ploutos' = wealth).

questions.stem: A person who is present in two different places at the same time (an impossible claim)
questions.explanation: D is correct. OMNIPRESENT = present everywhere at once (or seemingly so). Root: Latin 'omni' (all) + 'praesens' (being present). The definition describes someone claiming to be in two places simultaneously — the one-word substitute is OMNIPRESENT. Trap: Ubiquitous = seems to be everywhere at the same time (very close but slightly less specific to simultaneous physical presence); Omniscient = all-knowing ('scire' = to know); Ambidextrous = able to use both hands with equal skill.

questions.stem: A disease that spreads quickly over a large area and affects many people
questions.explanation: C is correct. PANDEMIC = a disease outbreak that spreads across countries or continents, affecting a large number of people worldwide. Root: Greek 'pan' (all) + 'demos' (people). Trap: Epidemic = an outbreak widespread within a community or region (not necessarily global — 'epi' = upon, 'demos' = people); Endemic = a disease regularly found in a particular area or region ('en-' = within); Contagion = the spreading of a disease through contact (process, not scale).

questions.stem: An inscription on a tombstone in memory of a dead person
questions.explanation: D is correct. EPITAPH = words written on a tombstone in memory of a deceased person. Root: Greek 'epi' (upon) + 'taphos' (tomb). Trap: Epilogue = a section at the end of a book or play ('logos' = word/speech); Eulogy = a spoken tribute to a recently deceased person (spoken at a funeral, not carved in stone); Epithet = a word or phrase that describes or identifies a person ('epi' + 'tithenai' = to place upon, but applied to a living quality not a tombstone).
